question: Under an explicitly hypothetical independent random train/test split, how often would related Artemis II representations or bracket siblings cross partitions if grouping occurs at the wrong unit?
terminal_objective: Turn the four-unit archive result into a decision-relevant AI evaluation guard without claiming that any existing analysis is contaminated.
method: Use the exact Stage 10L three-product-per-exposure parity and Stage 10J three- versus five-exposure action census. For independent Bernoulli assignment with train probability p, compute group-crossing probability as 1 - p^n - (1-p)^n at the product and exposure levels; compare with action-level grouping, which crosses zero actions by construction.
authority: Private local deterministic modeling only. No pixels, model training, publication, outreach, claim about an actual split, performance effect, archive defect, scientific result, or priority.
claim_ceiling: Stage 10M may establish expected related-group crossing under the frozen independent Bernoulli split model for the verified complete-action cohort. It may show why product-, exposure-, and action-level splits are different evaluation designs. It cannot claim observed leakage, contamination of any actual pipeline, byte-identical representations, identical bracket siblings, universal sufficiency of action grouping, statistical significance, performance impact, archive defect, image content, or global novelty or priority.

next_step_logic.if_group_crossing_is_material_across_sce: Keep action identity as the minimum split key for image-model evaluation on the verified cohort; add target, time, or scene grouping when the task creates broader dependence.
next_step_logic.if_a_real_pipeline_is_proposed: Freeze its actual task, transformations, split algorithm, and leakage oracle before applying this hazard model.
next_step_logic.if_the_action_oracle_expands: Recompute the action-size distribution and every scenario before reuse.
next_step_logic.recheck_trigger: A real AI evaluation design, revised representation mapping, expanded action oracle, or evidence that task dependence operates at a broader or narrower unit.
